events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.50 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The trace settles the two elements that decide liability here. The surge rose between quote and trip start, 1× → 1.5× [F8][SURGE-2], and the surge log records that the rider was not notified in-app at or before pickup [F9][SURGE-1]. The only messages on the record are a 21:02 pickup note [F10], the driver's 21:03 arrival note [F11] and the rider's post-trip 21:18 fare query [F12]; none of them states the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare or a free-cancellation option, so reading the words confirms that SURGE-1's notice is not met [F13][SURGE-1 / §3.2][SURGE-2 / §3.3].

Because the whole difference comes from surge and nothing else, the amount is the surge differential alone: the quote was $12.00 at 1× on a surgeable subtotal of $9.00 [F6] and the charge $16.50 at 1.5× on the same $9.00 subtotal [F7][F4], giving "(1.5 − 1.0) × $9.00 = $4.50" [F8][SURGE-3]. No other component is in play: the record shows no excess-distance element, since the actual 1.9 km is 1.2 km shorter than the 3.1 km recommended route [F2], and the trip took exactly the estimated 13.0 min [F3], so nothing is refundable under RD-1/RD-2 and no tolls or add-on fees are recorded [F5].

The outcome row is therefore "surge rose, rider not notified" → refund_full of the surge differential, i.e. refund_partial of $4.50 [SURGE-2][SURGE-3]. This follows the rider's route-and-surge precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice), which refunded the differential, here sized exactly at $4.50 [F6][F8][PREC-1].

On path: the disputed item is $4.50, under $10, so the system rules finally under TH-1 and, for a fare item, TH-2 follows TH-1 [TH-1][TH-2]. The surge log shows the rider was not notified of the surge change, and the chat record (3 timestamped messages, all about pickup and a post-trip query) contains no notice of the new multiplier, no revised fare estimate and no mention of free cancellation.
No route deviation inflates the fare: the actual distance of 1.9 km is 1.2 km shorter than the 3.1 km optimal route, so the overcharge cannot be explained by extra distance or tolls.
The rider not being notified of the surge change means the full surge differential of $4.50 is refundable under SURGE-2, following the precedent of DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice).
The rider has no fraud flags and no disputes on record, so the standard confidence threshold applies rather than the raised 95% threshold.

weaknesses: The fare record gives no line-item breakdown (F5), so the exact allocation within the $16.50 depends on the surgeable subtotal of $9.00 (F6, F7); the driver may argue part of the difference is something other than surge.

No extra component can be charged on top of the disclosed differential: the fare record gives no line-item breakdown of the $16.50 (F5), and the trip was on time and under the recommended distance (F2, F3), so no waiting fee, add-on destination fee or excess-distance charge is recorded.

The rider's own chat history contains no question about or objection to price before or during the trip; the only fare-related message is post-trip at 21:18 (F12), and the rider instead used the chat at 21:02 for a pickup-location message (F10), which is not notice of fare or consent to any charge.
